questions.question: Which of these does NOT help prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Getting a full night of sleep before driving
Traveling with a passenger
Planning trips for times when you would normally be sleeping
Avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness

questions.correctAnswerText: Planning trips for times when you would normally be sleeping
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is very dangerous. To prevent drowsiness, get a full night of sleep before driving, have someone else ride with you to take turns driving, schedule trips when you are normally awake, and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness.

questions.question: What is a vehicle inspection report for?

options.text: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed
To make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
To hold drivers responsible for inspecting their vehicles
To plan the next five trips

questions.correctAnswerText: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets drivers tell the motor carrier about safety issues with the vehicle. Drivers should fill out a report after each day of driving. Write down any problems that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should not be more than:

options.text: 10 degrees
25 degrees
50 degrees
75 degrees

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees
questions.explanation: More than 10 degrees of steering wheel play (about 2 inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel) makes steering difficult.

questions.question: Passive railroad crossings are:

options.text: Controlled by flashing lights
Not controlled by any traffic control device
Have gates that lower when trains approach
Should never be crossed by a commercial truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Not controlled by any traffic control device
questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: Large combination vehicles take the longest to stop when:

options.text: Fully loaded
Partially loaded
Empty
Mostly loaded

questions.correctAnswerText: Empty
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. Less weight means less traction on the road.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Ignore the report and find any issues themselves
Take the vehicle to a mechanic
Read the report
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading the last inspection report, if one exists. The carrier should have already fixed any problems listed on it.

questions.question: If hazardous cargo is leaking, the driver should:

options.text: Drive to find a phone and call emergency services
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility
Park the vehicle and call emergency services
Continue driving to the destination

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and call emergency services
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, stop driving as soon as safely possible. Continuing to drive spreads the hazard. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with it, and get help.

questions.question: Manhole covers:

options.text: Can be open while driving
Must be closed while driving
Should never be used
Should be removed while driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be closed while driving
questions.explanation: Before driving a tank vehicle, make sure all valves and manhole covers are closed.

questions.question: When loading a tank with bulkheads, pay attention to:

options.text: Spreading the weight evenly
Insects coming out of the tank
Where the nozzle is placed
Other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Spreading the weight evenly
questions.explanation: Some tanks have bulkheads dividing them into smaller sections. When loading, distribute the weight evenly. Do not put too much weight on one end of the tank.

questions.question: Move over laws require drivers to:

options.text: Use the left lane
Leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing
Always use the left lane
Move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the side of the road, move out of that lane if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over, slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: If a tank is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn on flashers to warn other drivers.
Fix the leak right away.
Tell someone at the end of the trip.
Try to weld the leak shut.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the leak right away.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to transport liquids or gases in a tank with a leak. If you find a leak, fix it immediately.

questions.question: Flammable gases are classified as ____ hazards.

options.text: Class 1
Class 2
Class 4
Class 7

questions.correctAnswerText: Class 2
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, how should you position the tractor?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle in front of the trailer.
Directly in front of the trailer.
At a 30-degree angle in front of the trailer.
At a 60-degree angle in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle could move the trailer and break the landing gear.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
When you are carrying a passenger.
When you are carrying a heavy load.
When driving in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces braking. But on slippery roads, it can cause wheels to skid. Turn it off in wet, snowy, or icy conditions.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which problems should be fixed?

options.text: Missing brackets or clamps.
Broken pipes, muffler, or tailpipe.
Leaking parts.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Exhaust problems are serious because poisonous fumes can enter the cab. Check for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, stacks, brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts. Also check that exhaust parts are not rubbing against fuel parts or tires, and that they are not leaking.

questions.question: How should you park to leave safely?

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can pull forward to leave.
On the side of a road, not in a lot.
By backing into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. When possible, park so you can pull forward to exit your space.

questions.question: How must placards be placed?

options.text: In any way, as long as they are visible.
So words and numbers read from left to right.
Upside down.
Within three inches of other markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards must be positioned so words and numbers can be read from left to right. They must be at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: How should you choose your driving speed?

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive slightly below the posted limit.
Adjust your speed to match road and traffic conditions.
Drive as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed to match road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many fatal crashes. Always adjust your speed to match current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles enter the lane.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
Do not use your turn signal.
Never use the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives drivers you did not see time to move or honk their horn. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What do baffled tanks have?

options.text: They do not prevent front-to-back liquid surge.
Bulkheads with holes that let liquid move between tank sections.
A valve that removes air.
Features that make unloading easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bulkheads with holes that let liquid move between tank sections.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have bulkheads with holes to control liquid movement. These reduce front-to-back surge, but side-to-side surge can still happen.
